entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shedsu-nefertum was a High Priest of Ptah at the end of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt and beginning of the Twenty-second Dynasty. He was the son of the High Priest Ankhefensekhmet and the lady Tapeshenese, who was First Chief of the Harem of Ptah and Prophetess of Mut.





Shedsu-nefertum played a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the Egyptian state during a period of significant turmoil. He worked closely with the Pharaoh Ramses XI to ensure the continuation of the traditional Egyptian order and the preservation of the temples and cults of Ptah.





His legacy can be seen in the many temples and shrines that were built during his reign, including the temple of Ptah at Saqqara, which was dedicated to the worship of the god Ptah and the goddess Mut.
